title: Linkability of user movements via GPS and timestamps
description: Continuous collection of GPS and timestamp data allows the device to link multiple data points, enabling tracking of the user's movements over time.

title: Identifiability through unique sensor patterns
description: Sensor data such as heart rate and GPS may contain unique patterns that can identify the user even if anonymized.

title: Unauthorized interception of sensor data in transit
description: If the data flow between the user and device is not encrypted, sensor telemetry could be intercepted by third parties.

title: Unauthorized use of collected sensor data
description: The device may use collected data for purposes beyond the user's consent, such as sharing with third parties for advertising.

title: User unaware of continuous data collection
description: The user may not be fully informed about the extent of data collection, leading to unintended privacy risks.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: The device's data handling practices may not comply with regulations like GDPR, leading to legal risks.

title: Linkability via Device ID
description: Transmission of device ID allows linking sensor data (GPS, exercise sessions) to a specific user, enabling cross-session tracking.

title: Data Misuse for Secondary Purposes
description: Companion app may use GPS and exercise data beyond original consent (e.g., targeted advertising, third-party sharing).

title: User Unaware of Data Collection
description: The app collects GPS location data without explicit user consent or notification, leading to unawareness of data processing.

title: Data Interception in Transit
description: Location data transmitted between app and store could be intercepted by attackers if not encrypted.

title: Data Misuse Beyond Consent
description: Stored location data may be used for purposes not originally consented to by the user, such as profiling or third-party sharing.

title: Identifiability of Location Data
description: Location traces with timestamps can be linked to specific users, enabling identification and tracking.

title: Data used beyond original consent
description: Health Analytics Service may process location history for purposes beyond the original consent, such as commercial profiling or third-party sharing.
assumptions: Service has broad data usage policies not explicitly communicated to users.

title: Re-identification through data combination
description: Aggregating location history across sessions may enable re-identification of individuals through pattern analysis.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to infer unique movement patterns.

title: Linking data to create a profile
description: Combining location data points across sessions allows creation of detailed behavioral profiles.
assumptions: Analytics service retains and correlates historical data over time.

title: Unauthorized disclosure
description: Processed location patterns may be disclosed to third parties without user consent.
assumptions: Service has data-sharing agreements not transparent to users.

title: Unauthorized Access to Data in Transit
description: Health analytics data transmitted between P3 and P2 may be intercepted if not properly encrypted, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health insights.

title: Unauthorized Use of Inferred Health Insights
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) may use the received health analytics data for purposes beyond user consent, such as sharing with third parties or targeted advertising.

title: Re-identification of Users from Inferred Health Data
description: Inferred health insights generated by P3 may contain sufficient information to re-identify users, especially when combined with other data sources.

title: Lack of Transparency in Data Processing
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their health data is being analyzed by P3 and shared with P2, leading to unawareness of data usage.

title: Unauthorized access to stored health data
description: Cloud provider's inadequate access controls could allow unauthorized parties to access sensitive health and location data at rest.

title: Data misuse for secondary purposes
description: Cloud provider may use health data for their own analytics or commercial purposes beyond the original consent.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Cloud provider's jurisdiction may not comply with applicable data protection laws, leading to regulatory violations.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Unencrypted data in transit could be intercepted by malicious actors.
uncertainty_note: Assumes encryption is not properly implemented; typically cloud providers use encryption in transit.
